<content>
# Start the full Stage 4 distributed stack locally (PowerShell, Windows).
#
# Starts the four backend processes (identity, commerce, reviews, gateway) from
# the shared services venv, each on its tool-isolated port from
# stage4-runtime.json, against the real RabbitMQ broker running in WSL.
#
# The broker is assumed already running and provisioned (see the README note);
# this script does NOT start RabbitMQ. Service/broker addresses are environment
# based with defaults from stage4-runtime.json.
#
# Readiness is checked deterministically by polling each /health endpoint. Each
# started process id is recorded in .stage4-pids.json so stop-stack.ps1 can kill
# exactly the processes this script owns.
#
# Usage:
#   .\scripts\start-stack.ps1            # start backend services + gateway
#   .\scripts\start-stack.ps1 -Frontend # additionally start the frontend (Vite)

param(
    [switch]$Frontend
)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
$root = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot
$runtime = Get-Content (Join-Path $root "stage4-runtime.json") | ConvertFrom-Json
$python = Join-Path $root "services\.venv\Scripts\python.exe"

if (-not (Test-Path $python)) {
    throw "Shared venv not found at $python. Create it with scripts\setup.ps1 first."
}

# Deployment parameters from stage4-runtime.json -> environment.
$env:GATEWAY_PORT = $runtime.gateway_port
$env:IDENTITY_PORT = $runtime.identity_port
$env:COMMERCE_PORT = $runtime.commerce_port
$env:REVIEWS_PORT = $runtime.reviews_port
$env:FRONTEND_PORT = $runtime.frontend_port
$env:AMQP_URL = $runtime.amqp_url
$env:EVENT_NAMESPACE = $runtime.event_namespace
$env:IDENTITY_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:$($runtime.identity_port)"
$env:COMMERCE_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:$($runtime.commerce_port)"
$env:REVIEWS_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:$($runtime.reviews_port)"
# Per-service owned stores under services/<name>/.
$env:IDENTITY_DB_PATH = Join-Path $root "services\identity\identity.db"
$env:COMMERCE_DB_PATH = Join-Path $root "services\commerce\commerce.db"
$env:REVIEWS_DB_PATH = Join-Path $root "services\reviews\reviews.db"
$env:REVIEW_IMAGE_DIR = Join-Path $root "services\reviews\review_images"

$pids = @()

function Start-Service($name, $cwd, $port) {
    Write-Host "Starting $name on port $port..."
    $proc = Start-Process -FilePath $python `
        -ArgumentList @("-m", "uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", "127.0.0.1", "--port", "$port") `
        -WorkingDirectory $cwd -PassThru -NoNewWindow
    return $proc
}

function Wait-Healthy($name, $port) {
    $url = "http://127.0.0.1:$port/health"
    for ($i = 0; $i -lt 60; $i++) {
        try {
            $resp = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -UseBasicParsing -TimeoutSec 2
            if ($resp.StatusCode -eq 200) {
                Write-Host "  $name is ready."
                return
            }
        } catch { Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 500 }
    }
    throw "$name did not become healthy on port $port"
}

$identity = Start-Service "identity" (Join-Path $root "services\identity") $runtime.identity_port
$pids += $identity.Id
$commerce = Start-Service "commerce" (Join-Path $root "services\commerce") $runtime.commerce_port
$pids += $commerce.Id
$reviews = Start-Service "reviews" (Join-Path $root "services\reviews") $runtime.reviews_port
$pids += $reviews.Id

Wait-Healthy "identity" $runtime.identity_port
Wait-Healthy "commerce" $runtime.commerce_port
Wait-Healthy "reviews" $runtime.reviews_port

$gateway = Start-Service "gateway" (Join-Path $root "services\gateway") $runtime.gateway_port
$pids += $gateway.Id
Wait-Healthy "gateway" $runtime.gateway_port

if ($Frontend) {
    Write-Host "Starting frontend (Vite dev) on port $($runtime.frontend_port)..."
    $fe = Start-Process -FilePath "npm" `
        -ArgumentList @("run", "dev", "--", "--port", "$($runtime.frontend_port)", "--strictPort") `
        -WorkingDirectory (Join-Path $root "frontend") -PassThru -NoNewWindow
    $pids += $fe.Id
}

$pids | ConvertTo-Json | Set-Content (Join-Path $root ".stage4-pids.json")
Write-Host ""
Write-Host "Stage 4 stack is up."
Write-Host "  Gateway:  http://127.0.0.1:$($runtime.gateway_port)"
if ($Frontend) { Write-Host "  Frontend: http://127.0.0.1:$($runtime.frontend_port)" }
Write-Host "Stop it with: .\scripts\stop-stack.ps1"

</content>
</file>

<file name="c:\Users\jeron\OneDrive\Escritorio\uni\implementacion Ecommerce\Caso 3-Ecommerce\Etapa 4\Kiro\scripts\stop-stack.ps1" language="plaintext" >
<content>
# Stop the Stage 4 stack started by start-stack.ps1 (owned-process cleanup).
#
# Reads .stage4-pids.json and stops exactly those process ids (and their uvicorn
# child processes), then removes the pid file. It does NOT touch the RabbitMQ
# broker, which is managed independently in WSL.

$ErrorActionPreference = "SilentlyContinue"
$root = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot
$pidFile = Join-Path $root ".stage4-pids.json"

if (-not (Test-Path $pidFile)) {
    Write-Host "No .stage4-pids.json found; nothing to stop."
    return
}

$pids = Get-Content $pidFile | ConvertFrom-Json
foreach ($processId in $pids) {
    $proc = Get-Process -Id $processId -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    if ($proc) {
        Write-Host "Stopping process $processId ($($proc.ProcessName))..."
        # Kill the process tree so uvicorn reload/child workers also stop.
        taskkill /PID $processId /T /F | Out-Null
    }
}

Remove-Item $pidFile -Force
Write-Host "Stage 4 stack stopped."

</content>
</file>

### Exact setup and startup commands (PowerShell)

One-time setup of the shared services virtual environment:

```powershell
.\scripts\setup.ps1
```

Start the full backend stack (identity, commerce, reviews, gateway) with deterministic `/health` readiness checks:

```powershell
.\scripts\start-stack.ps1
```

Add the frontend (Vite dev server on port 18300) as well:

```powershell
.\scripts\start-stack.ps1 -Frontend
```

Open <http://localhost:18300>. The frontend calls the gateway at `http://localhost:18200`.

Stop everything this stack started (owned-process cleanup):

```powershell
.\scripts\stop-stack.ps1
```

### Exact testing / verification commands (PowerShell)

Per-service unit tests with a combined raw backend coverage report (`coverage.xml`, Cobertura):

```powershell
$env:COVERAGE_RCFILE = ".coveragerc"
Remove-Item .coverage* -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
foreach ($svc in @("contracts","identity","commerce","reviews","gateway")) {
  services\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m coverage run -p -m pytest "services\$svc\tests" -q
}
services\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m coverage combine
services\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m coverage xml -o coverage.xml
```

Real multi-process, real-broker acceptance suite (boots the four services against the live RabbitMQ and drives the gateway over HTTP — proves cross-process event propagation, duplicate-delivery idempotency, and consumer outage/recovery without losing the accepted change):

```powershell
$env:AMQP_URL = "amqp://ecommerce:stage4-demo@127.0.0.1:5672/stage4_kiro"
services\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests_e2e -q
```

> The acceptance suite **skips** (does not fail) if the broker is unreachable, so unit suites still run without RabbitMQ. A genuine acceptance run requires the broker; CI asserts its availability.

Frontend unit tests with a raw coverage report (`frontend/coverage/lcov.info`, LCOV) and the production build:

```powershell
cd frontend
npm install
npm run test:coverage
npm run build
```

Frontend E2E (Playwright boots the Stage 4 stack via `e2e/global-setup.ts` against the real broker, builds and previews the frontend pointed at the gateway, then drives Chromium):

```powershell
cd frontend
npx playwright install chromium
$env:AMQP_URL = "amqp://ecommerce:stage4-demo@127.0.0.1:5672/stage4_kiro"
npm run test:e2e
```

</content>

# Start the full Stage 4 distributed stack locally (PowerShell, Windows).
#
# Starts the four backend processes (identity, commerce, reviews, gateway) from
# the shared services venv, each on its tool-isolated port from
# stage4-runtime.json, against the real RabbitMQ broker running in WSL.
#
# The broker is assumed already running and provisioned (see the README note);
# this script does NOT start RabbitMQ. Service/broker addresses are environment
# based with defaults from stage4-runtime.json.
#
# Readiness is checked deterministically by polling each /health endpoint (and,
# for the frontend, its HTTP root). Each started process is recorded immediately
# in .stage4-pids.json -- with its process name and start time so stop-stack.ps1
# can guard against stale/reused PIDs and kill exactly the processes this script
# owns. If any step fails, the processes started so far are cleaned up before
# the error propagates (no orphaned partial-start children).
#
# All processes are launched hidden with their stdout/stderr redirected to log
# files under logs/; no -NoNewWindow console-handle inheritance is used.
#
# Usage:
#   .\scripts\start-stack.ps1            # start backend services + gateway
#   .\scripts\start-stack.ps1 -Frontend # additionally start the frontend (Vite)

param(
    [switch]$Frontend
)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
$root = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot
$runtime = Get-Content (Join-Path $root "stage4-runtime.json") | ConvertFrom-Json
$python = Join-Path $root "services\.venv\Scripts\python.exe"

if (-not (Test-Path $python)) {
    throw "Shared venv not found at $python. Create it with scripts\setup.ps1 first."
}

$logDir = Join-Path $root "logs"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $logDir -Force | Out-Null
$pidFile = Join-Path $root ".stage4-pids.json"

# Deployment parameters from stage4-runtime.json -> environment.
$env:GATEWAY_PORT = $runtime.gateway_port
$env:IDENTITY_PORT = $runtime.identity_port
$env:COMMERCE_PORT = $runtime.commerce_port
$env:REVIEWS_PORT = $runtime.reviews_port
$env:FRONTEND_PORT = $runtime.frontend_port
$env:AMQP_URL = $runtime.amqp_url
$env:EVENT_NAMESPACE = $runtime.event_namespace
$env:IDENTITY_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:$($runtime.identity_port)"
$env:COMMERCE_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:$($runtime.commerce_port)"
$env:REVIEWS_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:$($runtime.reviews_port)"
# Per-service owned stores under services/<name>/.
$env:IDENTITY_DB_PATH = Join-Path $root "services\identity\identity.db"
$env:COMMERCE_DB_PATH = Join-Path $root "services\commerce\commerce.db"
$env:REVIEWS_DB_PATH = Join-Path $root "services\reviews\reviews.db"
$env:REVIEW_IMAGE_DIR = Join-Path $root "services\reviews\review_images"

# Owned-process records: one entry per spawned process, carrying enough identity
# (pid + process name + start time) for stop-stack.ps1 to reject stale/reused PIDs.
$owned = [System.Collections.ArrayList]::new()

function Save-Owned {
    # Persist the owned-process records immediately so a crash mid-start still
    # leaves a pid file the user (or stop-stack) can act on.
    $owned | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 4 | Set-Content $pidFile
}

function Register-Owned($name, $proc) {
    $record = [ordered]@{
        name        = $name
        pid         = $proc.Id
        processName = $proc.ProcessName
        startTime   = $proc.StartTime.ToString("o")
    }
    [void]$owned.Add($record)
    Save-Owned
}

function Stop-Owned {
    # Best-effort cleanup of every process started so far (used on failure).
    foreach ($record in $owned) {
        $p = Get-Process -Id $record.pid -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
        if ($p) {
            taskkill /PID $record.pid /T /F 2>$null | Out-Null
        }
    }
}

function Start-BackendService($name, $cwd, $port) {
    Write-Host "Starting $name on port $port..."
    $outLog = Join-Path $logDir "$name.out.log"
    $errLog = Join-Path $logDir "$name.err.log"
    $proc = Start-Process -FilePath $python `
        -ArgumentList @("-m", "uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", "127.0.0.1", "--port", "$port") `
        -WorkingDirectory $cwd -PassThru -WindowStyle Hidden `
        -RedirectStandardOutput $outLog -RedirectStandardError $errLog
    Register-Owned $name $proc
    return $proc
}

function Start-Frontend($cwd, $port) {
    Write-Host "Starting frontend (Vite dev) on port $port..."
    # npm.cmd is a batch shim that Start-Process cannot exec directly on Windows
    # (it raises "%1 is not a valid Win32 application"). Launch the installed
    # node executable against Vite's local JS entry instead, quoting paths with
    # spaces so a workspace under e.g. "OneDrive\Escritorio\..." still resolves.
    $node = (Get-Command node -ErrorAction Stop).Source
    $viteEntry = Join-Path $cwd "node_modules\vite\bin\vite.js"
    if (-not (Test-Path $viteEntry)) {
        throw "Vite entry not found at $viteEntry. Run 'npm install' in frontend first."
    }
    $outLog = Join-Path $logDir "frontend.out.log"
    $errLog = Join-Path $logDir "frontend.err.log"
    $proc = Start-Process -FilePath $node `
        -ArgumentList @("`"$viteEntry`"", "--port", "$port", "--strictPort") `
        -WorkingDirectory $cwd -PassThru -WindowStyle Hidden `
        -RedirectStandardOutput $outLog -RedirectStandardError $errLog
    Register-Owned "frontend" $proc
    return $proc
}

function Wait-Ready($name, $url) {
    for ($i = 0; $i -lt 60; $i++) {
        try {
            $resp = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -UseBasicParsing -TimeoutSec 2
            if ($resp.StatusCode -eq 200) {
                Write-Host "  $name is ready."
                return
            }
        } catch { Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 500 }
    }
    throw "$name did not become ready at $url"
}

function Wait-Healthy($name, $port) {
    Wait-Ready $name "http://127.0.0.1:$port/health"

function Start-Frontend($cwd, $port) {
    Write-Host "Starting frontend (Vite dev) on port $port..."
    # npm.cmd is a batch shim that Start-Process cannot exec directly on Windows
    # (it raises "%1 is not a valid Win32 application"). Launch the installed
    # node executable against Vite's local JS entry instead, quoting paths with
    # spaces so a workspace under e.g. "OneDrive\Escritorio\..." still resolves.
    $node = (Get-Command node -ErrorAction Stop).Source
    $viteEntry = Join-Path $cwd "node_modules\vite\bin\vite.js"
    if (-not (Test-Path $viteEntry)) {
        throw "Vite entry not found at $viteEntry. Run 'npm install' in frontend first."
    }
    $outLog = Join-Path $logDir "frontend.out.log"
    $errLog = Join-Path $logDir "frontend.err.log"
    $proc = Start-Process -FilePath $node `
        -ArgumentList @("`"$viteEntry`"", "--port", "$port", "--strictPort") `
        -WorkingDirectory $cwd -PassThru -WindowStyle Hidden `
        -RedirectStandardOutput $outLog -RedirectStandardError $errLog
    Register-Owned "frontend" $proc
    return $proc
}

function Wait-Ready($name, $url) {
    for ($i = 0; $i -lt 60; $i++) {
        try {
            $resp = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -UseBasicParsing -TimeoutSec 2
            if ($resp.StatusCode -eq 200) {
                Write-Host "  $name is ready."
                return
            }
        } catch { Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 500 }
    }
    throw "$name did not become ready at $url"
}

function Wait-Healthy($name, $port) {
    Wait-Ready $name "http://127.0.0.1:$port/health"
}

try {
    Start-BackendService "identity" (Join-Path $root "services\identity") $runtime.identity_port | Out-Null
    Start-BackendService "commerce" (Join-Path $root "services\commerce") $runtime.commerce_port | Out-Null
    Start-BackendService "reviews" (Join-Path $root "services\reviews") $runtime.reviews_port | Out-Null

    Wait-Healthy "identity" $runtime.identity_port
    Wait-Healthy "commerce" $runtime.commerce_port
    Wait-Healthy "reviews" $runtime.reviews_port

    Start-BackendService "gateway" (Join-Path $root "services\gateway") $runtime.gateway_port | Out-Null
    Wait-Healthy "gateway" $runtime.gateway_port

    if ($Frontend) {
        Start-Frontend (Join-Path $root "frontend") $runtime.frontend_port | Out-Null
        Wait-Ready "frontend" "http://127.0.0.1:$($runtime.frontend_port)/"
    }
}
catch {
    Write-Host "Startup failed: $($_.Exception.Message)" -ForegroundColor Red
    Write-Host "Cleaning up partially started processes..."
    Stop-Owned
    if (Test-Path $pidFile) { Remove-Item $pidFile -Force }
    throw
}

Write-Host "Stage 4 stack is up."
Write-Host "  Gateway:  http://127.0.0.1:$($runtime.gateway_port)"

# Stop the Stage 4 stack started by start-stack.ps1 (owned-process cleanup).
#
# Reads .stage4-pids.json and stops exactly those process ids (and their uvicorn
# child processes), then removes the pid file. It does NOT touch the RabbitMQ
# broker, which is managed independently in WSL.

$ErrorActionPreference = "SilentlyContinue"
$root = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot
$pidFile = Join-Path $root ".stage4-pids.json"

if (-not (Test-Path $pidFile)) {
    Write-Host "No .stage4-pids.json found; nothing to stop."
    return
}

$pids = Get-Content $pidFile | ConvertFrom-Json
foreach ($processId in $pids) {
    $proc = Get-Process -Id $processId -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    if ($proc) {
        Write-Host "Stopping process $processId ($($proc.ProcessName))..."
        # Kill the process tree so uvicorn reload/child workers also stop.
        taskkill /PID $processId /T /F | Out-Null
    }
}

Remove-Item $pidFile -Force
Write-Host "Stage 4 stack stopped."

content.oldText:
# Start the full Stage 4 distributed stack locally (PowerShell, Windows).
#
# Starts the four backend processes (identity, commerce, reviews, gateway) from
# the shared services venv, each on its tool-isolated port from
# stage4-runtime.json, against the real RabbitMQ broker running in WSL.
#
# The broker is assumed already running and provisioned (see the README note);
# this script does NOT start RabbitMQ. Service/broker addresses are environment
# based with defaults from stage4-runtime.json.
#
# Readiness is checked deterministically by polling each /health endpoint (and,
# for the frontend, its HTTP root). Each started process is recorded immediately
# in .stage4-pids.json -- with its process name and start time so stop-stack.ps1
# can guard against stale/reused PIDs and kill exactly the processes this script
# owns. If any step fails, the processes started so far are cleaned up before
# the error propagates (no orphaned partial-start children).
#
# All processes are launched hidden with their stdout/stderr redirected to log
# files under logs/; no -NoNewWindow console-handle inheritance is used.
#
# Usage:
#   .\scripts\start-stack.ps1            # start backend services + gateway
#   .\scripts\start-stack.ps1 -Frontend # additionally start the frontend (Vite)

param(
    [switch]$Frontend
)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
$root = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot
$runtime = Get-Content (Join-Path $root "stage4-runtime.json") | ConvertFrom-Json
$python = Join-Path $root "services\.venv\Scripts\python.exe"

if (-not (Test-Path $python)) {
    throw "Shared venv not found at $python. Create it with scripts\setup.ps1 first."
}

$logDir = Join-Path $root "logs"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $logDir -Force | Out-Null
$pidFile = Join-Path $root ".stage4-pids.json"

# Deployment parameters from stage4-runtime.json -> environment.
$env:GATEWAY_PORT = $runtime.gateway_port
$env:IDENTITY_PORT = $runtime.identity_port
$env:COMMERCE_PORT = $runtime.commerce_port
$env:REVIEWS_PORT = $runtime.reviews_port
$env:FRONTEND_PORT = $runtime.frontend_port
$env:AMQP_URL = $runtime.amqp_url
$env:EVENT_NAMESPACE = $runtime.event_namespace
$env:IDENTITY_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:$($runtime.identity_port)"
$env:COMMERCE_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:$($runtime.commerce_port)"
$env:REVIEWS_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:$($runtime.reviews_port)"
# Per-service owned stores under services/<name>/.
$env:IDENTITY_DB_PATH = Join-Path $root "services\identity\identity.db"
$env:COMMERCE_DB_PATH = Join-Path $root "services\commerce\commerce.db"
$env:REVIEWS_DB_PATH = Join-Path $root "services\reviews\reviews.db"
$env:REVIEW_IMAGE_DIR = Join-Path $root "services\reviews\review_images"

# Owned-process records: one entry per spawned process, carrying enough identity
# (pid + process name + start time) for stop-stack.ps1 to reject stale/reused PIDs.
$owned = [System.Collections.ArrayList]::new()

function Save-Owned {
    # Persist the owned-process records immediately so a crash mid-start still
    # leaves a pid file the user (or stop-stack) can act on.
    $owned | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 4 | Set-Content $pidFile
}

function Register-Owned($name, $proc) {
    $record = [ordered]@{
        name        = $name
        pid         = $proc.Id
        processName = $proc.ProcessName
        startTime   = $proc.StartTime.ToString("o")
    }
    [void]$owned.Add($record)
    Save-Owned
}

function Stop-Owned {
    # Best-effort cleanup of every process started so far (used on failure).
    foreach ($record in $owned) {
        $p = Get-Process -Id $record.pid -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
        if ($p) {
            taskkill /PID $record.pid /T /F 2>$null | Out-Null
        }
    }
}

function Start-BackendService($name, $cwd, $port) {
    Write-Host "Starting $name on port $port..."
    $outLog = Join-Path $logDir "$name.out.log"
    $errLog = Join-Path $logDir "$name.err.log"
    $proc = Start-Process -FilePath $python `
        -ArgumentList @("-m", "uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", "127.0.0.1", "--port", "$port") `
        -WorkingDirectory $cwd -PassThru -WindowStyle Hidden `
        -RedirectStandardOutput $outLog -RedirectStandardError $errLog
    Register-Owned $name $proc
    return $proc
}

function Start-Frontend($cwd, $port) {
    Write-Host "Starting frontend (Vite dev) on port $port..."
    # npm.cmd is a batch shim that Start-Process cannot exec directly on Windows
    # (it raises "%1 is not a valid Win32 application"). Launch the installed
    # node executable against Vite's local JS entry instead, quoting paths with
    # spaces so a workspace under e.g. "OneDrive\Escritorio\..." still resolves.
    $node = (Get-Command node -ErrorAction Stop).Source
    $viteEntry = Join-Path $cwd "node_modules\vite\bin\vite.js"
    if (-not (Test-Path $viteEntry)) {
        throw "Vite entry not found at $viteEntry. Run 'npm install' in frontend first."
    }
    $outLog = Join-Path $logDir "frontend.out.log"
    $errLog = Join-Path $logDir "frontend.err.log"
    $proc = Start-Process -FilePath $node `
        -ArgumentList @("`"$viteEntry`"", "--port", "$port", "--strictPort") `
        -WorkingDirectory $cwd -PassThru -WindowStyle Hidden `
        -RedirectStandardOutput $outLog -RedirectStandardError $errLog
    Register-Owned "frontend" $proc
    return $proc
}

function Wait-Ready($name, $url) {
    for ($i = 0; $i -lt 60; $i++) {
        try {
            $resp = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -UseBasicParsing -TimeoutSec 2
            if ($resp.StatusCode -eq 200) {
                Write-Host "  $name is ready."
                return
            }
        } catch { Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 500 }
    }
    throw "$name did not become ready at $url"
}

function Wait-Healthy($name, $port) {
    Wait-Ready $name "http://127.0.0.1:$port/health"
}

try {
    Start-BackendService "identity" (Join-Path $root "services\identity") $runtime.identity_port | Out-Null
    Start-BackendService "commerce" (Join-Path $root "services\commerce") $runtime.commerce_port | Out-Null
    Start-BackendService "reviews" (Join-Path $root "services\reviews") $runtime.reviews_port | Out-Null

    Wait-Healthy "identity" $runtime.identity_port
    Wait-Healthy "commerce" $runtime.commerce_port
    Wait-Healthy "reviews" $runtime.reviews_port

    Start-BackendService "gateway" (Join-Path $root "services\gateway") $runtime.gateway_port | Out-Null
    Wait-Healthy "gateway" $runtime.gateway_port

    if ($Frontend) {
        Start-Frontend (Join-Path $root "frontend") $runtime.frontend_port | Out-Null
        Wait-Ready "frontend" "http://127.0.0.1:$($runtime.frontend_port)/"
    }
}
catch {
    Write-Host "Startup failed: $($_.Exception.Message)" -ForegroundColor Red
    Write-Host "Cleaning up partially started processes..."
    Stop-Owned
    if (Test-Path $pidFile) { Remove-Item $pidFile -Force }
    throw
}

Write-Host ""
Write-Host "Stage 4 stack is up."
Write-Host "  Gateway:  http://127.0.0.1:$($runtime.gateway_port)"
if ($Frontend) { Write-Host "  Frontend: http://127.0.0.1:$($runtime.frontend_port)" }
Write-Host "Logs are under $logDir"
Write-Host "Stop it with: .\scripts\stop-stack.ps1"

# owns. If any step fails, the processes started so far are cleaned up before
# the error propagates (no orphaned partial-start children).
#
# All processes are launched hidden with their stdout/stderr redirected to log
# files under logs/; no -NoNewWindow console-handle inheritance is used.
#
# Usage:
#   .\scripts\start-stack.ps1            # start backend services + gateway
#   .\scripts\start-stack.ps1 -Frontend # additionally start the frontend (Vite)

param(
    [switch]$Frontend
)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
$root = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot
$runtime = Get-Content (Join-Path $root "stage4-runtime.json") | ConvertFrom-Json
$python = Join-Path $root "services\.venv\Scripts\python.exe"

if (-not (Test-Path $python)) {
    throw "Shared venv not found at $python. Create it with scripts\setup.ps1 first."
}

$logDir = Join-Path $root "logs"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $logDir -Force | Out-Null
$pidFile = Join-Path $root ".stage4-pids.json"

# Deployment parameters from stage4-runtime.json -> environment.
$env:GATEWAY_PORT = $runtime.gateway_port
$env:IDENTITY_PORT = $runtime.identity_port
$env:COMMERCE_PORT = $runtime.commerce_port
$env:REVIEWS_PORT = $runtime.reviews_port
$env:FRONTEND_PORT = $runtime.frontend_port
$env:AMQP_URL = $runtime.amqp_url
$env:EVENT_NAMESPACE = $runtime.event_namespace
$env:IDENTITY_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:$($runtime.identity_port)"
$env:COMMERCE_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:$($runtime.commerce_port)"
$env:REVIEWS_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:$($runtime.reviews_port)"
# Per-service owned stores under services/<name>/.
$env:IDENTITY_DB_PATH = Join-Path $root "services\identity\identity.db"
$env:COMMERCE_DB_PATH = Join-Path $root "services\commerce\commerce.db"
$env:REVIEWS_DB_PATH = Join-Path $root "services\reviews\reviews.db"
$env:REVIEW_IMAGE_DIR = Join-Path $root "services\reviews\review_images"

# Owned-process records: one entry per spawned process, carrying enough identity
# (pid + process name + start time) for stop-stack.ps1 to reject stale/reused PIDs.
$owned = [System.Collections.ArrayList]::new()

function Save-Owned {
    # Persist the owned-process records immediately so a crash mid-start still
    # leaves a pid file the user (or stop-stack) can act on.
    $owned | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 4 | Set-Content $pidFile
}

function Register-Owned($name, $proc) {
    $record = [ordered]@{
        name        = $name
        pid         = $proc.Id
        processName = $proc.ProcessName
        startTime   = $proc.StartTime.ToString("o")
    }
    [void]$owned.Add($record)
    Save-Owned
}

function Stop-Owned {
    # Best-effort cleanup of every process started so far (used on failure).
    foreach ($record in $owned) {
        $p = Get-Process -Id $record.pid -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
        if ($p) {
            taskkill /PID $record.pid /T /F 2>$null | Out-Null
        }
    }
}

function Start-BackendService($name, $cwd, $port) {
    Write-Host "Starting $name on port $port..."
    $outLog = Join-Path $logDir "$name.out.log"
    $errLog = Join-Path $logDir "$name.err.log"
    $proc = Start-Process -FilePath $python `
        -ArgumentList @("-m", "uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", "127.0.0.1", "--port", "$port") `
        -WorkingDirectory $cwd -PassThru -WindowStyle Hidden `
        -RedirectStandardOutput $outLog -RedirectStandardError $errLog
    Register-Owned $name $proc
    return $proc
}

function Start-Frontend($cwd, $port) {
    Write-Host "Starting frontend (Vite dev) on port $port..."
    # npm.cmd is a batch shim that Start-Process cannot exec directly on Windows
    # (it raises "%1 is not a valid Win32 application"). Launch the installed
    # node executable against Vite's local JS entry instead, quoting paths with
    # spaces so a workspace under e.g. "OneDrive\Escritorio\..." still resolves.
    $node = (Get-Command node -ErrorAction Stop).Source
    $viteEntry = Join-Path $cwd "node_modules\vite\bin\vite.js"
    if (-not (Test-Path $viteEntry)) {
        throw "Vite entry not found at $viteEntry. Run 'npm install' in frontend first."
    }
    $outLog = Join-Path $logDir "frontend.out.log"
    $errLog = Join-Path $logDir "frontend.err.log"
    # Bind Vite to 127.0.0.1 explicitly: its default "localhost" resolves to ::1
    # (IPv6) on this host, which the IPv4 readiness poll below never reaches.
    $proc = Start-Process -FilePath $node `
        -ArgumentList @("`"$viteEntry`"", "--host", "127.0.0.1", "--port", "$port", "--strictPort") `
        -WorkingDirectory $cwd -PassThru -WindowStyle Hidden `
        -RedirectStandardOutput $outLog -RedirectStandardError $errLog
    Register-Owned "frontend" $proc
    return $proc
}

function Wait-Ready($name, $url) {
    for ($i = 0; $i -lt 60; $i++) {
        try {
            $resp = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -UseBasicParsing -TimeoutSec 2
            if ($resp.StatusCode -eq 200) {
                Write-Host "  $name is ready."
                return
            }
        } catch { Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 500 }
    }
    throw "$name did not become ready at $url"
}

function Wait-Healthy($name, $port) {
    Wait-Ready $name "http://127.0.0.1:$port/health"
}

try {
    Start-BackendService "identity" (Join-Path $root "services\identity") $runtime.identity_port | Out-Null
    Start-BackendService "commerce" (Join-Path $root "services\commerce") $runtime.commerce_port | Out-Null
    Start-BackendService "reviews" (Join-Path $root "services\reviews") $runtime.reviews_port | Out-Null

    Wait-Healthy "identity" $runtime.identity_port
    Wait-Healthy "commerce" $runtime.commerce_port
    Wait-Healthy "reviews" $runtime.reviews_port

    Start-BackendService "gateway" (Join-Path $root "services\gateway") $runtime.gateway_port | Out-Null
    Wait-Healthy "gateway" $runtime.gateway_port

    if ($Frontend) {
        Start-Frontend (Join-Path $root "frontend") $runtime.frontend_port | Out-Null
        Wait-Ready "frontend" "http://127.0.0.1:$($runtime.frontend_port)/"
    }
}
catch {
    Write-Host "Startup failed: $($_.Exception.Message)" -ForegroundColor Red
    Write-Host "Cleaning up partially started processes..."
    Stop-Owned
    if (Test-Path $pidFile) { Remove-Item $pidFile -Force }
    throw
}

Write-Host ""
Write-Host "Stage 4 stack is up."
Write-Host "  Gateway:  http://127.0.0.1:$($runtime.gateway_port)"
if ($Frontend) { Write-Host "  Frontend: http://127.0.0.1:$($runtime.frontend_port)" }
Write-Host "Logs are under $logDir"
Write-Host "Stop it with: .\scripts\stop-stack.ps1"

    $proc = Start-Process -FilePath $node `
        -ArgumentList @("`"$viteEntry`"", "--host", "127.0.0.1", "--port", "$port", "--strictPort") `

content.oldText:
# E-Commerce Stage 1 + Stage 2 + Stage 3

This repository contains a demonstration e-commerce application generated for the SDD tools comparison. It consists of a React and TypeScript frontend and a Python and FastAPI backend.

**Stage 1** delivers the core purchasing journey: browse the catalog, manage a local cart, register or sign in, and complete a simulated checkout.

**Stage 2** adds **product reviews with images and moderation** on top of Stage 1, without changing the Stage 1 journey. A signed-in customer can submit a review (star rating, text, optional title, and up to three images) for a product; every review enters a moderation queue; a moderator approves or rejects it; and only approved reviews are shown publicly on the product together with an aggregate rating summary. See the native specification in `.kiro/specs/ecommerce-stage2/` (requirements, design, tasks) and the inherited Stage 1 spec in `.kiro/specs/ecommerce-stage1/`.

**Stage 3** adds **architecture and automated delivery verification** (Option A) on top of Stage 2, without changing any application behavior: real end-to-end (Playwright) tests against the running stack, a CI pipeline (install → test with coverage → build → E2E), reproducible multi-stage Docker builds with a one-command local orchestration, and bounded caching for the public catalog read endpoints. See the native specification in `.kiro/specs/ecommerce-stage3/` (requirements, design, tasks). The quickest way to run and verify Stage 3 is the [Stage 3 section below](#stage-3-e2e-tests-ci-containers-and-caching).

## Prerequisites

- Python 3.11 or later
- Node.js 18 or later
- npm

## Project structure

```text
backend/    FastAPI API, services, data access, and backend tests
frontend/   React application, client-side state, and frontend tests
.kiro/      Kiro specification artifacts
```

## Run the application

The backend and frontend must run in separate terminals.

### 1. Start the backend

Open a terminal in the repository root and run:

```powershell
cd backend
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install -r requirements.txt
uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000
```

On macOS or Linux, activate the virtual environment with:

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
```

The backend will be available at:

- API: <http://localhost:8000>
- Health check: <http://localhost:8000/health>
- Interactive API documentation: <http://localhost:8000/docs>

### 2. Start the frontend

Open a second terminal in the repository root and run:

```powershell
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open <http://localhost:5173> in a browser.

The frontend expects the backend to be running at `http://localhost:8000`.

## Run the tests

### Backend

With the backend virtual environment activated:

```powershell
cd backend
pytest
```

### Frontend

```powershell
cd frontend
npm test
```

## Build the frontend

To type-check the frontend and create a production build:

```powershell
cd frontend
npm run build
```

The generated production files will be placed in `frontend/dist`.

## Stage 2: reviews, images, and moderation

### How to try it

1. Start the backend and frontend as described above (two terminals). The backend seeds a demonstration moderator account automatically at startup.
2. In the browser, open a product's **View details** panel in the Catalog. The expanded panel shows the product's approved reviews, a rating summary, and — when you are signed in as a customer — a review submission form.
3. **Submit a review** as a customer: register or sign in on the **Account** view, then expand a product, choose a rating, write the review text (optionally a title), optionally attach up to three images, and submit. The review is created as `pending` and is not yet publicly visible.
4. **Moderate** the review: sign out, then sign in with the moderator credentials below and open the **Moderation** destination in the top navigation. The pending review appears in the queue with its product, rating, text, images, and author. Approve it to make it publicly visible (and counted in the rating summary) or reject it to keep it hidden.
5. Re-open the product's details as any visitor: approved reviews and the rating summary are now shown.

### Moderator demonstration credentials

A single built-in moderator account is seeded at backend startup so the moderation workflow can be demonstrated immediately:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Identifier | `moderator` |
| Password | `moderator123` |

These are a local-demo convenience defined in `backend/app/services/moderator_seed.py`. Sign in with them on the Account view; the **Moderation** view then becomes usable. A regular customer account cannot access moderation.

### Stage 2 endpoints (added additively over the Stage 1 six)

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/products/{id}/reviews` | Approved reviews + rating summary for a product |
| `POST` | `/products/{id}/reviews` | Submit a review (active customer session required) |
| `GET` | `/reviews/images/{imageId}` | Serve a stored review image |
| `GET` | `/moderation/reviews` | Pending moderation queue (moderator session required) |
| `POST` | `/moderation/reviews/{reviewId}/approve` | Approve a pending review (moderator) |
| `POST` | `/moderation/reviews/{reviewId}/reject` | Reject a pending review (moderator) |

## Important implementation notes

- The catalog, account, and review data use an in-process demonstration store; nothing is persisted durably across backend restarts.
- Review **image bytes** are the only on-disk artifact: they are written to the git-ignored folder `backend/app/data/review_images/` and served through the backend. No external object storage, CDN, or paid service is used.
- Review images are submitted as base64-encoded data in the JSON request, validated (type allow-list JPEG/PNG/GIF/WebP, max 2 MB, up to 3 per review), and only then stored.
- Moderation states are `pending`, `approved`, and `rejected`; a decision is terminal. A customer may submit at most one review per product, and submitted reviews cannot be edited or deleted. These and other delegated decisions are documented as assumptions A1–A8 in `.kiro/specs/ecommerce-stage2/requirements.md`.
- The cart and session state are kept in frontend memory and are reset when the page is reloaded.
- Checkout is simulated. No real payment is processed and no order is persisted.
- All interface text, code, comments, and specifications are in English.

## Stage 3: E2E tests, CI, containers, and caching

Stage 3 is additive: the nine existing endpoints' request/response bodies are unchanged except for added cache/freshness response headers, and the frontend journeys and views are unchanged. The native Stage 3 spec lives in `.kiro/specs/ecommerce-stage3/`.

### Demo / moderator credentials

The seeded moderator account (used by the review-lifecycle E2E test and by manual moderation) is unchanged from Stage 2:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Identifier | `moderator` |
| Password | `moderator123` |

### Exact startup commands (PowerShell)

Run the backend and frontend in two terminals from the repository root.

Backend (first terminal):

```powershell
cd backend
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install -r requirements.txt
uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000
```

Frontend (second terminal):

```powershell
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open <http://localhost:5173>. The frontend calls the backend at `http://localhost:8000`.

### Exact testing / verification commands (PowerShell)

Backend tests with a raw coverage report (`backend/coverage.xml`, Cobertura):

```powershell
cd backend
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install coverage
coverage run -m pytest
coverage xml -o coverage.xml
```

Frontend unit/integration tests with a raw coverage report (`frontend/coverage/lcov.info`, LCOV):

```powershell
cd frontend
npm run test:coverage
```

Frontend production build (type-check + Vite build into `frontend/dist`):

```powershell
cd frontend
npm run build
```

Real end-to-end tests (Playwright boots the real backend and the production build, then drives Chromium). Run once to install the browser, then run the suite:

```powershell
cd frontend
npx playwright install chromium
npm run test:e2e
```

The E2E suite covers three journeys: the Stage 1 purchasing journey, the Stage 2 review lifecycle (submit → pending/hidden → moderator approval → public), and a moderation access-denied check for a regular customer. The Playwright config starts `uvicorn` from `backend/` (using `backend/.venv` when present) on port 8000 and `vite preview` on port 4173; if a server cannot start, the run fails loudly rather than passing against a dead stack.

### Bounded public API caching

- Only the two session-independent public catalog reads are cached: `GET /products` and `GET /products/{id}`.
- The cache is in-process and bounded by both a per-entry TTL and a maximum entry count. Defaults: TTL `30s` (`CATALOG_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`, set `0` to disable), max entries `256` (`CATALOG_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES`).
- Cached responses carry `X-Cache: HIT|MISS` and `Cache-Control: public, max-age=<ttl>`. Session-varying and authenticated responses — `GET /products/{id}/reviews` (it includes the caller's own review), `/auth/*`, and `/moderation/*` — are marked `Cache-Control: no-store` and are **never** shared-cached, so no per-user data can leak between callers.
- **Invalidation / freshness:** the review-listing endpoint is intentionally uncached, so a newly approved review is immediately publicly visible; a moderation approve/reject additionally calls a cache-invalidation hook. Stale catalog entries cannot outlive their TTL.

Example (observe the cache headers):

```powershell
# First call: X-Cache: MISS ; second call within the TTL: X-Cache: HIT
(Invoke-WebRequest http://localhost:8000/products -UseBasicParsing).Headers['X-Cache']
(Invoke-WebRequest http://localhost:8000/products -UseBasicParsing).Headers['X-Cache']
```

### Containers and one-command local orchestration

Reproducible multi-stage builds are provided: `backend/Dockerfile` (`python:3.11-slim` builder + slim runtime, uvicorn on container port 8000) and `frontend/Dockerfile` (`node:20-alpine` build stage → `nginx:1.27-alpine` serving the static build on container port 80). A single orchestration command starts both with a user-defined bridge network and a `/health` readiness healthcheck on the backend:

```powershell
docker compose up --build
```

This publishes the backend on host port 8000 and the frontend on host port 8080 (open <http://localhost:8080>). Because the backend is published on host 8000, the frontend's existing `http://localhost:8000` API base URL keeps working unchanged. No external or paid service is used and nothing is deployed.

> **Runtime note (honest limitation):** Docker was **not available** in the environment where this stage was validated (`docker` is not on PATH). The `Dockerfile`s, `nginx.conf`, and `docker-compose.yml` were validated by inspection and are exercised by the CI definition, but **a local container run was not executed and is not claimed.** Run `docker compose up --build` on a machine with Docker installed to start the containerized stack.

### Continuous integration

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on push and pull request: it installs backend and frontend dependencies, runs the backend tests producing `coverage.xml`, runs the frontend unit tests producing `lcov.info`, builds the frontend, installs the Playwright browser, runs the E2E suite against the real stack, and uploads the coverage reports and the Playwright report as artifacts. It does **not** publish or deploy to any external infrastructure.

> **Coverage note:** the coverage reports (`backend/coverage.xml`, `frontend/coverage/lcov.info`) are produced for later quality analysis. No coverage target is prescribed and no unexecuted check is claimed as passed.

## Stage 4: microservices + real RabbitMQ (Option A)

Stage 4 is an **architectural breaking change**: the Stage 3 monolithic backend is migrated into **independently running Python/FastAPI microservices** coordinated by a **real RabbitMQ broker**. No end-user behavior changes — the Stage 1 purchasing journey and the Stage 2 review/moderation workflow are preserved exactly. The native Stage 4 spec lives in `.kiro/specs/ecommerce-stage4/` (requirements, design, contracts, tasks).

### Architecture

Four independent processes, each with its own store, plus a thin HTTP gateway that preserves the nine-endpoint frontend contract:

| Process | Port | Owns | Store |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| gateway | 18200 | frontend contract, session cookie, edge catalog cache | — (routes over HTTP) |
| identity | 18201 | accounts, auth, signed tokens | `services/identity/identity.db` |
| commerce | 18202 | catalog, checkout, **public review projection** | `services/commerce/commerce.db` |
| reviews | 18203 | review submission, images, moderation, **outbox** | `services/reviews/reviews.db` + `review_images/` |

Moderation events flow over RabbitMQ: on approve/reject the **reviews** service writes the decision and an **outbox** row in one SQLite transaction; a background relay publishes to the durable topic exchange `stage4.kiro.events` with **publisher confirms**; the **commerce** consumer applies it to its public projection with **manual acks**, **idempotency** (keyed on `eventId`), **bounded retry + dead-letter queue**, and **reconnect backoff**. Semantics are **at-least-once + idempotent** — exactly-once is **not** claimed. Approved reviews become public within a small, bounded eventual-consistency window (seconds locally).

No service trusts a client-supplied role header: identity issues an HMAC-signed bearer token whose role claim is inside the signature, and the gateway binds it to an httpOnly session cookie and forwards it downstream.

### Demo / moderator credentials

Unchanged and seeded automatically by the identity service at startup:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Identifier | `moderator` |
| Password | `moderator123` |

Regular customers register on the Account view. A customer cannot access moderation (403).

### Runtime parameters

Ports and broker come from `stage4-runtime.json` (tool-isolated): gateway `18200`, identity `18201`, commerce `18202`, reviews `18203`, frontend `18300`, AMQP `amqp://ecommerce:stage4-demo@127.0.0.1:5672/stage4_kiro`, vhost `stage4_kiro`, event namespace `stage4.kiro`. All are overridable by environment variables.

The RabbitMQ broker runs locally in **Ubuntu/WSL** (Docker is unavailable on this host). It is already provisioned with the user/vhost above. If you need to (re)provision it, run `./scripts/provision-broker.ps1` (requires `rabbitmqctl` privileges in WSL).

### Exact setup and startup commands (PowerShell)

One-time setup of the shared services virtual environment:

```powershell
.\scripts\setup.ps1
```

Start the full backend stack (identity, commerce, reviews, gateway) with deterministic `/health` readiness checks:

```powershell
.\scripts\start-stack.ps1
```

Add the frontend (Vite dev server on port 18300) as well:

```powershell
.\scripts\start-stack.ps1 -Frontend
```

Open <http://localhost:18300>. The frontend calls the gateway at `http://localhost:18200`.

Stop everything this stack started (owned-process cleanup):

```powershell
.\scripts\stop-stack.ps1
```

### Exact testing / verification commands (PowerShell)

Per-service unit tests with a combined raw backend coverage report (`coverage.xml`, Cobertura):

```powershell
$env:COVERAGE_RCFILE = ".coveragerc"
Remove-Item .coverage* -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
foreach ($svc in @("contracts","identity","commerce","reviews","gateway")) {
  services\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m coverage run -p -m pytest "services\$svc\tests" -q
}
services\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m coverage combine
services\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m coverage xml -o coverage.xml
```

Real multi-process, real-broker acceptance suite (boots the four services against the live RabbitMQ and drives the gateway over HTTP — proves cross-process event propagation, duplicate-delivery idempotency, and consumer outage/recovery without losing the accepted change):

```powershell
$env:AMQP_URL = "amqp://ecommerce:stage4-demo@127.0.0.1:5672/stage4_kiro"
services\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests_e2e -q
```

> The acceptance suite **skips** (does not fail) if the broker is unreachable, so unit suites still run without RabbitMQ. A genuine acceptance run requires the broker; CI asserts its availability.

Frontend unit tests with a raw coverage report (`frontend/coverage/lcov.info`, LCOV) and the production build:

```powershell
cd frontend
npm install
npm run test:coverage
npm run build
```

Frontend E2E (Playwright boots the Stage 4 stack via `e2e/global-setup.ts` against the real broker, builds and previews the frontend pointed at the gateway, then drives Chromium):

```powershell
cd frontend
npx playwright install chromium
$env:AMQP_URL = "amqp://ecommerce:stage4-demo@127.0.0.1:5672/stage4_kiro"
npm run test:e2e
```

### Containers and CI

`docker-compose.stage4.yml` defines the full stack: RabbitMQ, the three services, the gateway, and the frontend, on a user-defined bridge network with a broker healthcheck. `services/Dockerfile` is a shared multi-stage image for the Python services; the frontend reuses its multi-stage `frontend/Dockerfile` with a `VITE_API_BASE_URL` build arg.

```powershell
docker compose -f docker-compose.stage4.yml up --build
```

> **Runtime note (honest limitation):** Docker was **not available** in the environment where Stage 4 was validated (`docker` is not on PATH; RabbitMQ runs in WSL). The Compose file and Dockerfiles were validated by inspection and are exercised by the CI definition, but **a local container run was NOT executed and is not claimed.** Stage 4 was validated **natively** against the provisioned WSL broker with the commands above. Run the Compose command on a machine with Docker installed to start the containerized stack.

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs the distributed pipeline on push and pull request: it installs the services venv, runs the per-service unit tests producing `coverage.xml`, runs the real-broker acceptance suite against a RabbitMQ **service container**, runs the frontend unit tests producing `lcov.info`, builds the frontend, and runs the Playwright E2E. It uploads coverage and the Playwright report as artifacts and does **not** deploy.

# E-Commerce Stage 1 + Stage 2 + Stage 3

This repository contains a demonstration e-commerce application generated for the SDD tools comparison. It consists of a React and TypeScript frontend and a Python and FastAPI backend.

**Stage 1** delivers the core purchasing journey: browse the catalog, manage a local cart, register or sign in, and complete a simulated checkout.

**Stage 2** adds **product reviews with images and moderation** on top of Stage 1, without changing the Stage 1 journey. A signed-in customer can submit a review (star rating, text, optional title, and up to three images) for a product; every review enters a moderation queue; a moderator approves or rejects it; and only approved reviews are shown publicly on the product together with an aggregate rating summary. See the native specification in `.kiro/specs/ecommerce-stage2/` (requirements, design, tasks) and the inherited Stage 1 spec in `.kiro/specs/ecommerce-stage1/`.

**Stage 3** adds **architecture and automated delivery verification** (Option A) on top of Stage 2, without changing any application behavior: real end-to-end (Playwright) tests against the running stack, a CI pipeline (install → test with coverage → build → E2E), reproducible multi-stage Docker builds with a one-command local orchestration, and bounded caching for the public catalog read endpoints. See the native specification in `.kiro/specs/ecommerce-stage3/` (requirements, design, tasks). The quickest way to run and verify Stage 3 is the [Stage 3 section below](#stage-3-e2e-tests-ci-containers-and-caching).

## Prerequisites

- Python 3.11 or later
- Node.js 18 or later
- npm

## Project structure

```text
backend/    FastAPI API, services, data access, and backend tests
frontend/   React application, client-side state, and frontend tests
.kiro/      Kiro specification artifacts
```

## Run the application

The backend and frontend must run in separate terminals.

### 1. Start the backend

Open a terminal in the repository root and run:

```powershell
cd backend
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install -r requirements.txt
uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000
```

On macOS or Linux, activate the virtual environment with:

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
```

The backend will be available at:

- API: <http://localhost:8000>
- Health check: <http://localhost:8000/health>
- Interactive API documentation: <http://localhost:8000/docs>

### 2. Start the frontend

Open a second terminal in the repository root and run:

```powershell
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open <http://localhost:5173> in a browser.

The frontend expects the backend to be running at `http://localhost:8000`.

## Run the tests

### Backend

With the backend virtual environment activated:

```powershell
cd backend
pytest
```

### Frontend

```powershell
cd frontend
npm test
```

## Build the frontend

To type-check the frontend and create a production build:

```powershell
cd frontend
npm run build
```

The generated production files will be placed in `frontend/dist`.

## Stage 2: reviews, images, and moderation

### How to try it

1. Start the backend and frontend as described above (two terminals). The backend seeds a demonstration moderator account automatically at startup.
2. In the browser, open a product's **View details** panel in the Catalog. The expanded panel shows the product's approved reviews, a rating summary, and — when you are signed in as a customer — a review submission form.
3. **Submit a review** as a customer: register or sign in on the **Account** view, then expand a product, choose a rating, write the review text (optionally a title), optionally attach up to three images, and submit. The review is created as `pending` and is not yet publicly visible.
4. **Moderate** the review: sign out, then sign in with the moderator credentials below and open the **Moderation** destination in the top navigation. The pending review appears in the queue with its product, rating, text, images, and author. Approve it to make it publicly visible (and counted in the rating summary) or reject it to keep it hidden.
5. Re-open the product's details as any visitor: approved reviews and the rating summary are now shown.

### Moderator demonstration credentials

A single built-in moderator account is seeded at backend startup so the moderation workflow can be demonstrated immediately:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Identifier | `moderator` |
| Password | `moderator123` |

These are a local-demo convenience defined in `backend/app/services/moderator_seed.py`. Sign in with them on the Account view; the **Moderation** view then becomes usable. A regular customer account cannot access moderation.

### Stage 2 endpoints (added additively over the Stage 1 six)

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/products/{id}/reviews` | Approved reviews + rating summary for a product |
| `POST` | `/products/{id}/reviews` | Submit a review (active customer session required) |
| `GET` | `/reviews/images/{imageId}` | Serve a stored review image |
| `GET` | `/moderation/reviews` | Pending moderation queue (moderator session required) |
| `POST` | `/moderation/reviews/{reviewId}/approve` | Approve a pending review (moderator) |
| `POST` | `/moderation/reviews/{reviewId}/reject` | Reject a pending review (moderator) |

## Important implementation notes

- The catalog, account, and review data use an in-process demonstration store; nothing is persisted durably across backend restarts.
- Review **image bytes** are the only on-disk artifact: they are written to the git-ignored folder `backend/app/data/review_images/` and served through the backend. No external object storage, CDN, or paid service is used.
- Review images are submitted as base64-encoded data in the JSON request, validated (type allow-list JPEG/PNG/GIF/WebP, max 2 MB, up to 3 per review), and only then stored.
- Moderation states are `pending`, `approved`, and `rejected`; a decision is terminal. A customer may submit at most one review per product, and submitted reviews cannot be edited or deleted. These and other delegated decisions are documented as assumptions A1–A8 in `.kiro/specs/ecommerce-stage2/requirements.md`.
- The cart and session state are kept in frontend memory and are reset when the page is reloaded.
- Checkout is simulated. No real payment is processed and no order is persisted.
- All interface text, code, comments, and specifications are in English.

## Stage 3: E2E tests, CI, containers, and caching

Stage 3 is additive: the nine existing endpoints' request/response bodies are unchanged except for added cache/freshness response headers, and the frontend journeys and views are unchanged. The native Stage 3 spec lives in `.kiro/specs/ecommerce-stage3/`.

### Demo / moderator credentials

The seeded moderator account (used by the review-lifecycle E2E test and by manual moderation) is unchanged from Stage 2:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Identifier | `moderator` |
| Password | `moderator123` |

### Exact startup commands (PowerShell)

Run the backend and frontend in two terminals from the repository root.

Backend (first terminal):

```powershell
cd backend
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install -r requirements.txt
uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000
```

Frontend (second terminal):

```powershell
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open <http://localhost:5173>. The frontend calls the backend at `http://localhost:8000`.

### Exact testing / verification commands (PowerShell)

Backend tests with a raw coverage report (`backend/coverage.xml`, Cobertura):

```powershell
cd backend
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install coverage
coverage run -m pytest
coverage xml -o coverage.xml
```

Frontend unit/integration tests with a raw coverage report (`frontend/coverage/lcov.info`, LCOV):

```powershell
cd frontend
npm run test:coverage
```

Frontend production build (type-check + Vite build into `frontend/dist`):

```powershell
cd frontend
npm run build
```

Real end-to-end tests (Playwright boots the real backend and the production build, then drives Chromium). Run once to install the browser, then run the suite:

```powershell
cd frontend
npx playwright install chromium
npm run test:e2e
```

The E2E suite covers three journeys: the Stage 1 purchasing journey, the Stage 2 review lifecycle (submit → pending/hidden → moderator approval → public), and a moderation access-denied check for a regular customer. The Playwright config starts `uvicorn` from `backend/` (using `backend/.venv` when present) on port 8000 and `vite preview` on port 4173; if a server cannot start, the run fails loudly rather than passing against a dead stack.

### Bounded public API caching

- Only the two session-independent public catalog reads are cached: `GET /products` and `GET /products/{id}`.
- The cache is in-process and bounded by both a per-entry TTL and a maximum entry count. Defaults: TTL `30s` (`CATALOG_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`, set `0` to disable), max entries `256` (`CATALOG_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES`).
- Cached responses carry `X-Cache: HIT|MISS` and `Cache-Control: public, max-age=<ttl>`. Session-varying and authenticated responses — `GET /products/{id}/reviews` (it includes the caller's own review), `/auth/*`, and `/moderation/*` — are marked `Cache-Control: no-store` and are **never** shared-cached, so no per-user data can leak between callers.
- **Invalidation / freshness:** the review-listing endpoint is intentionally uncached, so a newly approved review is immediately publicly visible; a moderation approve/reject additionally calls a cache-invalidation hook. Stale catalog entries cannot outlive their TTL.

Example (observe the cache headers):

```powershell
# First call: X-Cache: MISS ; second call within the TTL: X-Cache: HIT
(Invoke-WebRequest http://localhost:8000/products -UseBasicParsing).Headers['X-Cache']
(Invoke-WebRequest http://localhost:8000/products -UseBasicParsing).Headers['X-Cache']
```

### Containers and one-command local orchestration

Reproducible multi-stage builds are provided: `backend/Dockerfile` (`python:3.11-slim` builder + slim runtime, uvicorn on container port 8000) and `frontend/Dockerfile` (`node:20-alpine` build stage → `nginx:1.27-alpine` serving the static build on container port 80). A single orchestration command starts both with a user-defined bridge network and a `/health` readiness healthcheck on the backend:

```powershell
docker compose up --build
```

This publishes the backend on host port 8000 and the frontend on host port 8080 (open <http://localhost:8080>). Because the backend is published on host 8000, the frontend's existing `http://localhost:8000` API base URL keeps working unchanged. No external or paid service is used and nothing is deployed.

> **Runtime note (honest limitation):** Docker was **not available** in the environment where this stage was validated (`docker` is not on PATH). The `Dockerfile`s, `nginx.conf`, and `docker-compose.yml` were validated by inspection and are exercised by the CI definition, but **a local container run was not executed and is not claimed.** Run `docker compose up --build` on a machine with Docker installed to start the containerized stack.

### Continuous integration

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on push and pull request: it installs backend and frontend dependencies, runs the backend tests producing `coverage.xml`, runs the frontend unit tests producing `lcov.info`, builds the frontend, installs the Playwright browser, runs the E2E suite against the real stack, and uploads the coverage reports and the Playwright report as artifacts. It does **not** publish or deploy to any external infrastructure.

> **Coverage note:** the coverage reports (`backend/coverage.xml`, `frontend/coverage/lcov.info`) are produced for later quality analysis. No coverage target is prescribed and no unexecuted check is claimed as passed.

Stage 4 is an **architectural breaking change**: the Stage 3 monolithic backend is migrated into **independently running Python/FastAPI microservices** coordinated by a **real RabbitMQ broker**. Four independent processes, each with its own store, plus a thin HTTP gateway that preserves the nine-endpoint frontend contract:

| Process | Port | Owns | Store |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| gateway | 18200 | frontend contract, session cookie, edge catalog cache | — (routes over HTTP) |
| identity | 18201 | accounts, auth, signed tokens | `services/identity/identity.db` |
| commerce | 18202 | catalog, checkout, **public review projection** | `services/commerce/commerce.db` |
| reviews | 18203 | review submission, images, moderation, **outbox** | `services/reviews/reviews.db` + `review_images/` |

Moderation events flow over RabbitMQ: on approve/reject the **reviews** service writes the decision and an **outbox** row in one SQLite transaction; a background relay publishes to the durable topic exchange `stage4.kiro.events` with **publisher confirms**; the **commerce** consumer applies it to its public projection with **manual acks**, **idempotency** (keyed on `eventId`), **bounded retry + dead-letter queue**, and **reconnect backoff**. Semantics are **at-least-once + idempotent** — exactly-once is **not** claimed. Approved reviews become public within a small, bounded eventual-consistency window (seconds locally).

No service trusts a client-supplied role header: identity issues an HMAC-signed bearer token whose role claim is inside the signature, and the gateway binds it to an httpOnly session cookie and forwards it downstream.

### Demo / moderator credentials

Unchanged and seeded automatically by the identity service at startup:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Identifier | `moderator` |
| Password | `moderator123` |

Regular customers register on the Account view. A customer cannot access moderation (403).

### Runtime parameters

Ports and broker come from `stage4-runtime.json` (tool-isolated): gateway `18200`, identity `18201`, commerce `18202`, reviews `18203`, frontend `18300`, AMQP `amqp://ecommerce:stage4-demo@127.0.0.1:5672/stage4_kiro`, vhost `stage4_kiro`, event namespace `stage4.kiro`. All are overridable by environment variables.

The RabbitMQ broker runs locally in **Ubuntu/WSL** (Docker is unavailable on this host). It is already provisioned with the user/vhost above. If you need to (re)provision it, run `./scripts/provision-broker.ps1` (requires `rabbitmqctl` privileges in WSL).

### Exact setup and startup commands (PowerShell)

One-time setup of the shared services virtual environment:

```powershell
.\scripts\setup.ps1
```

Start the full backend stack (identity, commerce, reviews, gateway) with deterministic `/health` readiness checks:

```powershell
.\scripts\start-stack.ps1
```

Add the frontend (Vite dev server on port 18300) as well:

```powershell
.\scripts\start-stack.ps1 -Frontend
```

Open <http://localhost:18300>. The frontend calls the gateway at `http://localhost:18200`.

All services and the frontend are launched **hidden**, with their stdout/stderr redirected to per-process log files under `logs/` (e.g. `logs/gateway.err.log`, `logs/frontend.out.log`). The frontend is started by invoking the installed `node` against Vite's local JS entry (`frontend/node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js`) rather than `npm` — on Windows `Start-Process npm` fails with `%1 is not a valid Win32 application` because `npm.cmd` is a batch shim. Each owned process id is recorded in `.stage4-pids.json` immediately on spawn, and a failed start cleans up any partially started children.

Stop everything this stack started (owned-process cleanup):

```powershell
.\scripts\stop-stack.ps1
```

Per-service unit tests with a combined raw backend coverage report (`coverage.xml`, Cobertura):

```powershell
$env:COVERAGE_RCFILE = ".coveragerc"
Remove-Item .coverage* -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
foreach ($svc in @("contracts","identity","commerce","reviews","gateway")) {
  services\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m coverage run -p -m pytest "services\$svc\tests" -q

services\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m coverage xml -o coverage.xml
```

```powershell
$env:AMQP_URL = "amqp://ecommerce:stage4-demo@127.0.0.1:5672/stage4_kiro"
services\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests_e2e -q
```

> The acceptance suite **skips** (does not fail) if the broker is unreachable, so unit suites still run without RabbitMQ. A genuine acceptance run requires the broker; CI asserts its availability.

Frontend unit tests with a raw coverage report (`frontend/coverage/lcov.info`, LCOV) and the production build:

```powershell
cd frontend
npm install
npm run test:coverage
npm run build
```

Frontend E2E (Playwright boots the Stage 4 stack via `e2e/global-setup.ts` against the real broker, builds and previews the frontend pointed at the gateway, then drives Chromium):

```powershell
cd frontend
npx playwright install chromium
$env:AMQP_URL = "amqp://ecommerce:stage4-demo@127.0.0.1:5672/stage4_kiro"
npm run test:e2e
```

`docker-compose.stage4.yml` defines the full stack: RabbitMQ, the three services, the gateway, and the frontend, on a user-defined bridge network with a broker healthcheck. `services/Dockerfile` is a shared multi-stage image for the Python services; the frontend reuses its multi-stage `frontend/Dockerfile` with a `VITE_API_BASE_URL` build arg.

```powershell

```

**Stage 1** delivers the core purchasing journey: browse the catalog, manage a local cart, register or sign in, and complete a simulated checkout.

**Stage 2** adds **product reviews with images and moderation** on top of Stage 1, without changing the Stage 1 journey. A signed-in customer can submit a review (star rating, text, optional title, and up to three images) for a product; every review enters a moderation queue; a moderator approves or rejects it; and only approved reviews are shown publicly on the product together with an aggregate rating summary. See the native specification in `.kiro/specs/ecommerce-stage2/` (requirements, design, tasks) and the inherited Stage 1 spec in `.kiro/specs/ecommerce-stage1/`.

**Stage 3** adds **architecture and automated delivery verification** (Option A) on top of Stage 2, without changing any application behavior: real end-to-end (Playwright) tests against the running stack, a CI pipeline (install → test with coverage → build → E2E), reproducible multi-stage Docker builds with a one-command local orchestration, and bounded caching for the public catalog read endpoints. See the native specification in `.kiro/specs/ecommerce-stage3/` (requirements, design, tasks). The quickest way to run and verify Stage 3 is the [Stage 3 section below](#stage-3-e2e-tests-ci-containers-and-caching).

## Prerequisites

- Python 3.11 or later
- Node.js 18 or later
- npm

## Project structure

```text
backend/    FastAPI API, services, data access, and backend tests
frontend/   React application, client-side state, and frontend tests
.kiro/      Kiro specification artifacts
```

## Run the application

The backend and frontend must run in separate terminals.

### 1. Start the backend

Open a terminal in the repository root and run:

```powershell
cd backend
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install -r requirements.txt
uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000
```

On macOS or Linux, activate the virtual environment with:

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
```

The backend will be available at:

- API: <http://localhost:8000>
- Health check: <http://localhost:8000/health>
- Interactive API documentation: <http://localhost:8000/docs>

### 2. Start the frontend

Open a second terminal in the repository root and run:

```powershell
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open <http://localhost:5173> in a browser.

The frontend expects the backend to be running at `http://localhost:8000`.

```powershell
cd backend
pytest
```

### Frontend

```powershell
cd frontend
npm test
```

```powershell
cd frontend
npm run build
```

The generated production files will be placed in `frontend/dist`.

1. Start the backend and frontend as described above (two terminals). The backend seeds a demonstration moderator account automatically at startup.
2. In the browser, open a product's **View details** panel in the Catalog. The expanded panel shows the product's approved reviews, a rating summary, and — when you are signed in as a customer — a review submission form.
3. **Submit a review** as a customer: register or sign in on the **Account** view, then expand a product, choose a rating, write the review text (optionally a title), optionally attach up to three images, and submit. The review is created as `pending` and is not yet publicly visible.
4. **Moderate** the review: sign out, then sign in with the moderator credentials below and open the **Moderation** destination in the top navigation. The pending review appears in the queue with its product, rating, text, images, and author. Approve it to make it publicly visible (and counted in the rating summary) or reject it to keep it hidden.
5. Re-open the product's details as any visitor: approved reviews and the rating summary are now shown.

### Moderator demonstration credentials

A single built-in moderator account is seeded at backend startup so the moderation workflow can be demonstrated immediately:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Identifier | `moderator` |
| Password | `moderator123` |

These are a local-demo convenience defined in `backend/app/services/moderator_seed.py`. Sign in with them on the Account view; the **Moderation** view then becomes usable. A regular customer account cannot access moderation.

### Stage 2 endpoints (added additively over the Stage 1 six)

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/products/{id}/reviews` | Approved reviews + rating summary for a product |
| `POST` | `/products/{id}/reviews` | Submit a review (active customer session required) |
| `GET` | `/reviews/images/{imageId}` | Serve a stored review image |
| `GET` | `/moderation/reviews` | Pending moderation queue (moderator session required) |
| `POST` | `/moderation/reviews/{reviewId}/approve` | Approve a pending review (moderator) |
| `POST` | `/moderation/reviews/{reviewId}/reject` | Reject a pending review (moderator) |

Real multi-process, real-broker acceptance suite (boots the four services against the live RabbitMQ and drives the gateway over HTTP — proves cross-process event propagation, duplicate-delivery idempotency, and consumer outage/recovery without losing the accepted change):

```powershell
$env:AMQP_URL = "amqp://ecommerce:stage4-demo@127.0.0.1:5672/stage4_kiro"
services\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests_e2e -q
```

> The acceptance suite **skips** (does not fail) if the broker is unreachable, so unit suites still run without RabbitMQ. A genuine acceptance run requires the broker; CI asserts its availability.

Frontend unit tests with a raw coverage report (`frontend/coverage/lcov.info`, LCOV) and the production build:

```powershell
cd frontend
npm install
npm run test:coverage
npm run build
```

Frontend E2E (Playwright boots the Stage 4 stack via `e2e/global-setup.ts` against the real broker, builds and previews the frontend pointed at the gateway, then drives Chromium):

```powershell
cd frontend
npx playwright install chromium
$env:AMQP_URL = "amqp://ecommerce:stage4-demo@127.0.0.1:5672/stage4_kiro"
npm run test:e2e
```

### Containers and CI

`docker-compose.stage4.yml` defines the full stack: RabbitMQ, the three services, the gateway, and the frontend, on a user-defined bridge network with a broker healthcheck. `services/Dockerfile` is a shared multi-stage image for the Python services; the frontend reuses its multi-stage `frontend/Dockerfile` with a `VITE_API_BASE_URL` build arg.

```powershell
docker compose -f docker-compose.stage4.yml up --build
```

> **Runtime note (honest limitation):** Docker was **not available** in the environment where Stage 4 was validated (`docker` is not on PATH; RabbitMQ runs in WSL). The Compose file and Dockerfiles were validated by inspection and are exercised by the CI definition, but **a local container run was NOT executed and is not claimed.** Stage 4 was validated **natively** against the provisioned WSL broker with the commands above. Run the Compose command on a machine with Docker installed to start the containerized stack.

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs the distributed pipeline on push and pull request: it installs the services venv, runs the per-service unit tests producing `coverage.xml`, runs the real-broker acceptance suite against a RabbitMQ **service container**, runs the frontend unit tests producing `lcov.info`, builds the frontend, and runs the Playwright E2E. It uploads coverage and the Playwright report as artifacts and does **not** deploy.

> **Coverage note:** the coverage reports (`coverage.xml`, `frontend/coverage/lcov.info`) are produced for later analysis. No coverage target is prescribed and no unexecuted check is claimed as passed.

### What the monolith (`backend/`) is now

The inherited `backend/` monolith and its Stage 1–3 specs are retained for reference and keep their own unit tests, but it is **no longer the running system**. The Stage 4 scripts and Compose start the services under `services/` instead.

    Register-Owned $name $proc

function Start-Frontend($cwd, $port) {
    Write-Host "Starting frontend (Vite dev) on port $port..."
    # npm.cmd is a batch shim that Start-Process cannot exec directly on Windows
    # (it raises "%1 is not a valid Win32 application"). Launch the installed
    # node executable against Vite's local JS entry instead, quoting paths with
    # spaces so a workspace under e.g. "OneDrive\Escritorio\..." still resolves.
    $node = (Get-Command node -ErrorAction Stop).Source
    $viteEntry = Join-Path $cwd "node_modules\vite\bin\vite.js"
    if (-not (Test-Path $viteEntry)) {
        throw "Vite entry not found at $viteEntry. Run 'npm install' in frontend first."
    }
    $outLog = Join-Path $logDir "frontend.out.log"
    $errLog = Join-Path $logDir "frontend.err.log"
    # Bind Vite to 127.0.0.1 explicitly: its default "localhost" resolves to ::1
    # (IPv6) on this host, which the IPv4 readiness poll below never reaches.
    $proc = Start-Process -FilePath $node `
        -ArgumentList @("`"$viteEntry`"", "--host", "127.0.0.1", "--port", "$port", "--strictPort") `
        -WorkingDirectory $cwd -PassThru -WindowStyle Hidden `
        -RedirectStandardOutput $outLog -RedirectStandardError $errLog
    Register-Owned "frontend" $proc
    return $proc
}

function Wait-Ready($name, $url) {
    for ($i = 0; $i -lt 60; $i++) {
        try {
            $resp = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -UseBasicParsing -TimeoutSec 2
            if ($resp.StatusCode -eq 200) {
                Write-Host "  $name is ready."
                return
            }
        } catch { Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 500 }
    }
    throw "$name did not become ready at $url"
}

function Wait-Healthy($name, $port) {
    Wait-Ready $name "http://127.0.0.1:$port/health"
}

try {
    Start-BackendService "identity" (Join-Path $root "services\identity") $runtime.identity_port | Out-Null
    Start-BackendService "commerce" (Join-Path $root "services\commerce") $runtime.commerce_port | Out-Null
    Start-BackendService "reviews" (Join-Path $root "services\reviews") $runtime.reviews_port | Out-Null

    Wait-Healthy "identity" $runtime.identity_port
    Wait-Healthy "commerce" $runtime.commerce_port
    Wait-Healthy "reviews" $runtime.reviews_port

    Start-BackendService "gateway" (Join-Path $root "services\gateway") $runtime.gateway_port | Out-Null
    Wait-Healthy "gateway" $runtime.gateway_port

    if ($Frontend) {
        Start-Frontend (Join-Path $root "frontend") $runtime.frontend_port | Out-Null
        Wait-Ready "frontend" "http://127.0.0.1:$($runtime.frontend_port)/"
    }
}
catch {
    Write-Host "Startup failed: $($_.Exception.Message)" -ForegroundColor Red
    Write-Host "Cleaning up partially started processes..."
    Stop-Owned
    if (Test-Path $pidFile) { Remove-Item $pidFile -Force }
    throw
}
</content>

## Summary

The verified Windows launcher defect is fixed, and the exact documented command is proven end-to-end.

**Root cause(s) found and corrected in `scripts/start-stack.ps1`:**
1. **`Start-Process -FilePath "npm"` → `%1 is not a valid Win32 application`** — `npm.cmd` is a batch shim that Windows cannot exec directly. Now the frontend launches the installed `node` executable (resolved at runtime via `Get-Command node`) against the local Vite JS entry `frontend/node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js`, with the entry path quoted to survive the spaces in the workspace path.
2. **Vite bound to `localhost` (IPv6 `::1`)** so an IPv4 `127.0.0.1` readiness poll never succeeded. Added `--host 127.0.0.1` so readiness and the browser URL are deterministic.
3. **Partial-start orphans** — every process is now registered in `.stage4-pids.json` *immediately* on spawn; a `try/catch` runs `Stop-Owned` to clean up all started children if any later step throws.
4. **Console-handle inheritance** — replaced `-NoNewWindow` with `-WindowStyle Hidden` plus `-RedirectStandardOutput`/`-RedirectStandardError` into per-process `logs/*.log` for all services and the frontend.
5. **Frontend HTTP readiness** is now verified in addition to all four backend `/health` endpoints.

**Spec/docs updated before code:** added task 6.5 to `.kiro/specs/ecommerce-stage4/tasks.md`; updated the README Stage 4 start/stop sections.

**Actual launcher test result** (exact documented command `.\scripts\start-stack.ps1 -Frontend`, then `.\scripts\stop-stack.ps1`):
- Launcher printed `frontend is ready.` and `Stage 4 stack is up.` with an empty error log.
- Gateway `http://127.0.0.1:18200/health` → `200 {"status":"ok"}`.
- Frontend `http://127.0.0.1:18300/` → `200`, 560 bytes (Vite index).
- All five ports (18200–18203, 18300) LISTENING; `.stage4-pids.json` recorded all five owned processes with identity.
- After `stop-stack.ps1`: all five matched by identity and killed, pid file removed, all five ports `-`, all five PIDs `GONE`.

I did not touch the shared RabbitMQ broker, sibling workspaces, or any passing coverage/build/browser outputs; temporary verification artifacts (`logs/`, capture logs) were cleaned up.
